objects.original: Finite-dimensional real inner-product normed E, its Borel measurable structure, actual standard Gaussian gamma_E, and real L2 equivalence classes.
objects.reconstructed: The reconstruction explicitly names the same compatible real Hilbert geometry, Gaussian probability and quotient L2 carrier.
objects.evidence: The five structure binders match the source objects; no replacement measure or unrelated feature carrier appears.

domains.original: Finite S subset of natural degrees, real coefficient function c, and ambient w.
domains.reconstructed: Finite s, arbitrary c:N->R, all w in E; same L2 carrier.
domains.evidence: Off-support coefficients are irrelevant; empty support, zero degree and signed/zero coefficients are allowed in both.

quantifiers.original: Define one F_(S,c)(w) for every S,c,w.
quantifiers.reconstructed: The type is Finset(N) -> (N->R) -> E -> L2, with all parameters arbitrary.
quantifiers.evidence: There is no hidden choice of support or ordering, and no existential feature family.

assumptions.original: No parity, positivity, unit-direction, normalization or infinite-series convergence premise.
assumptions.reconstructed: Only finiteness of s and real coefficients are required; empty sum is zero.
assumptions.evidence: A finite scalar sum in L2 uses vector-space operations and does not require multiplying two L2 functions.

conclusion.original: The definition is sum_(j in S)c(j)h_j(w) in L2.
conclusion.reconstructed: The exact finite linear combination, equivalently the class of the literal finite Hermite sum.
conclusion.evidence: Linearity of quotient addition/scalar multiplication justifies the equivalent representative formulation without extra analytic assumptions.

scopes.original: Finite sum in one actual Gaussian L2 space; not an infinite feature limit.
scopes.reconstructed: Both sum and scalar multiplication are in L2; no series limit or alternative carrier.
scopes.evidence: The finite body matches the reviewed module and compact definition rendering.

constant_dependencies.original: Arbitrary real coefficients c(j), unchanged and unsquared in the definition.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The same c(j) multiplies each class; no normalization or bound.
constant_dependencies.evidence: Squaring coefficients belongs only to the later Gram theorem, not this definition.
